chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said:

I was with him guiding him, so I entered the bathhouse and saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) applying Noura. So Abu Baseer approached him and greeted him, so he said: 'O Abu Baseer, apply Noura.' He said, 'I only applied it first thing yesterday, and it is the third day.' So he said: 'Do you not know that it is a cleanser? So apply it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on applying Noura (lime paste) in the bathhouse according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Abu Baseer to apply *Noura* (lime paste) in the bathhouse, clarifying its status as a purifier (*tahoor*) despite the companion's hesitation regarding its recent application. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the ritual purity of lime paste, thereby validating its use in personal hygiene and ablution contexts. It reflects the practical emphasis on cleanliness (*taharah*) as an integral component of faith and spiritual preparation.
